entries.614a42466525c0d3: In February 2025, the company announced "INPEX Vision 2035 'Realizing a Responsible Energy Transition'". Here the company presented its long-term strategy toward 2035 and also formulated a medium-term management plan for the 3 years from 2025 to 2027, presenting its immediate specific initiatives and targets. In the same February 2025, Japan's 7th Strategic Energy Plan was presented, and the targets for the self-development ratio of oil and natural gas (50% or more in 2030 and 60% or more in 2040) were maintained.

entries.66af0d17aab7b8ae: A category covering renewable energy and electricity-related businesses, CCS and hydrogen businesses, crude oil sales agency and brokerage businesses, and others; the company notes that it is a business segment not included in reportable segments. External revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥17,176 million (down 3.0% year on year), broken down into crude oil ¥9,783 million, other ¥7,182 million, and natural gas ¥211 million. Segment profit was a loss of △¥28,795 million (the previous year was also a loss of △¥14,545 million), exploration and development investment was ¥26.5 billion, and electricity generation was 2,424 million kWh (up 16.4% year on year). In renewable energy, the company has INPEX Australia Mirai Energies Pty Ltd and INPEX Renewable Energy Australia Pty Ltd, which provide funding to development and operation businesses in Australia; Potentia Energy Group Pty Ltd in Australia (equity interest 50.00%); companies involved in the Sarulla, Muara Laboh and Rantau Dedap geothermal blocks in Indonesia; INPEX Geothermal Development Co., Ltd., which develops and manages geothermal power generation businesses in Japan and overseas; and INPEX Europe Limited, which develops and manages offshore wind businesses in Europe. In CCS, the company has Shutoken CCS Co., Ltd. (equity interest 85.00%), which conducts the transport and storage of CO2 in the CCS business in the Tokyo metropolitan area. The company states that, for the transition to net zero, it is important to select appropriate means according to regional circumstances and the stage of transition, and that, in addition to introducing renewable energy, introducing CCS to existing oil and natural gas production facilities and using hydrogen and ammonia are also realistic pathways for the energy transition. Because it is not a reportable segment, it is placed last rather than in a position below Domestic O&G based on external revenue.

entries.9d67a5bfadd11f7a: The Ichthys gas and condensate field (blocks WA-50-L/WA-51-L) in Western Australia and surrounding exploration, which the company positions as the group's main operator project. External revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥315,069 million (down 15.6% year on year), consisting of natural gas of ¥196,676 million (sales volume 306,630 million CF) and crude oil of ¥118,392 million (11,147 thousand barrels); within the group, it is a rare segment in which natural gas revenue exceeds crude oil. The company attributes the decline in revenue to lower sales prices, and states that segment profit (profit attributable to owners of the parent) increased to ¥270,801 million (up 9.1%) owing to factors such as lower exploration expenses. This profit exceeds that of Other Projects, whose external revenue is nearly 5 times larger, and is the largest among the reporting segments. Production was 12,049 thousand barrels of crude oil (33 thousand barrels per day) and 337,122 million CF of natural gas (924 million CF per day), totaling 77,193 thousand BOE. Facilities are production facilities and other assets held by INPEX Ichthys Pty Ltd (the company's equity interest 67.82%), with a book value of ¥1,770,688 million and land of 4,510 thousand ㎡. Ichthys LNG Pty Ltd (equity interest 67.82%), a jointly controlled entity, is responsible for laying and operating the subsea gas pipeline from the gas field to the onshore LNG plant in Darwin, constructing and operating the LNG plant, and selling LNG, liquefied petroleum gas and condensate, and it borrows project finance from domestic and overseas export credit agencies and commercial banks with itself as the borrower. Other operating income for the period includes ¥34.7 billion from the transfer from equity to profit or loss of the accumulated foreign currency translation differences of foreign operations, arising from a partial paid capital reduction of INPEX Holdings Australia Pty Ltd, which forms part of the Ichthys LNG Project.

entries.a0cef5d980549f08: A segment that brings together overseas projects in Australia (excluding Ichthys), Southeast Asia, Europe, Abu Dhabi, etc. External revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,486,928 million (down 10.3% year on year), broken down into crude oil ¥1,399,457 million (sales volume 133,271 thousand barrels), natural gas ¥82,329 million (sales volume 60,028 million CF), and other ¥5,141 million. The company attributes this decline in revenue to lower sales prices. Segment profit (profit for the year attributable to owners of the parent) was ¥131,790 million (down 20.5%), and although external revenue is nearly five times that of the Ichthys Project, its profit is below that of the Ichthys Project. This is because corporate income tax expense is large at △¥702,992 million, and the gap from the pre-tax stage is a feature of this segment. The main companies are Japan Oil Development Co., Ltd., which handles the Upper Zakum, Sata and Umm Al Dalkh oil fields off Abu Dhabi (for the fiscal year ended December 2025: revenue ¥579,882 million, profit before tax ¥373,211 million, profit for the year ¥46,631 million), and JODCO Onshore Limited, which holds the Abu Dhabi onshore block (revenue ¥409,306 million, profit before tax ¥255,869 million, profit for the year ¥25,778 million), both of which account for more than 10% of consolidated revenue. Other companies include JODCO Lower Zakum Limited, for the Lower Zakum offshore oil field off Abu Dhabi; INPEX North Caspian Sea Co., Ltd. (interest ratio 7.56%), for the North Caspian Sea offshore block in Kazakhstan; MI Berau B.V. (equity interest 44.00%), for the Berau block in West Papua Province, Indonesia, and the Tangguh LNG Project; INPEX Oil & Gas Australia Pty Ltd, for the Prelude gas field in Australia and others; INPEX Saul Oil Co., Ltd., in East Timor; and INPEX Masela Co., Ltd., for the Masela block in the Arafura Sea, Indonesia. The company also provides funding, through INPEX BTC Pipeline, Ltd., for the construction and operation of an oil pipeline running from Baku in Azerbaijan through Georgia and Tbilisi to Ceyhan in Turkey. In the current period, the company recorded impairment losses of ¥21,405 million and reversal of impairment losses of ¥41,253 million.

entries.ad413a2e58a661ed: The company states that the form of sales of oil and natural gas produced in Japan and overseas is almost entirely wholesale to oil wholesalers, electric power companies, city gas businesses, and others, and that the number of customers is naturally limited. It also states that the number of customers has been decreasing due to corporate consolidation from industry reorganization and other factors, and that the share of transactions with a single customer tends to become relatively higher. Even so, there is no external customer accounting for 10% or more of consolidated revenue. Revenue by region in the fiscal year ended December 2025, based on final destination and customer, is Asia ¥704,108 million (South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, etc.), Japan ¥625,880 million, China ¥341,261 million, Europe ¥233,951 million (Italy, etc.), and Other ¥106,150 million (Australia, etc.), and areas other than Japan account for nearly 7 tenths. Part of the natural gas is under long-term supply contracts, and the total transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations whose initially expected remaining period exceeds 1 year is ¥286,087 million (within 1 year ¥51,830 million; more than 1 year and within 5 years ¥117,096 million; more than 5 years ¥117,160 million). Regarding medium- to long-term energy demand, the company assumes that the trend of sustained growth in energy demand will not change, due to the expansion of the world population and economic growth centered on emerging countries, and states that, for demand for oil and natural gas, and particularly natural gas demand, firm demand is expected over the medium to long term, centered on Asia.
